dailyRead: The ceasefire the whole book was warned about arrived - and the oil premium is unwinding. Regional mediators (Pakistan, Qatar, Turkey, Egypt) have tabled a 10-day truce reopening BOTH Hormuz lanes - the southern Omani route free of Iranian attacks and the northern Iranian route free of the US blockade - with a middle-corridor concept and Iranian barrels re-entering the market. Crude collapsed ~5% intraday to a $83.19 low (WTI ~$84, Brent ~$86), compounded by a fresh US inventory build. Every oil-linked leg reverses at once: CAD's terms-of-trade premium is gutted (the clearest loser), gold and silver bled off the haven bid ($4,046 / $57.68), and the yen gets a fundamental oil-relief tailwind - though USD/JPY still sits ~163.8 because the dollar is firm into the Fed. The story is now policy, not oil: tomorrow (Wed Jul 29) delivers a twin binary - the FOMC (CME ~66% hold / ~34% hike, up from ~16% on Jul 23; September ~82% priced) AND Australia Q2 CPI (consensus trimmed mean ~3.7%). Cleanest lean flips to USD/CAD LONG (HIGH); USOIL flips to SHORT (MED); XAU/XAG downgraded from LONG to RANGE (short tilt); and last week's cleanest trade, CAD/JPY LONG, is dead - flipped to RANGE (short tilt). The caveat that caps the whole de-escalation trade: the US is demanding a LONGER truce than 10 days, so this is a proposal, not a signed deal - a collapse re-arms every oil leg in a session.

geopolitics: The pivot: de-escalation, and the oil trade is one-way down. Regional mediators - Pakistan, Qatar, Turkey and Egypt - have tabled a 10-day ceasefire reopening BOTH Strait of Hormuz lanes: the southern route through Omani waters free of Iranian attacks, and the northern route through Iranian waters free of the US blockade, with a proposed middle corridor where vessels transit and Iran collects reasonable service fees. Iranian barrels are re-entering the market. Crude, which last week printed the cycle high on a 12th strike night, collapsed ~5% intraday to a $83.19 low (WTI ~$84, Brent ~$86), compounded by a fresh US inventory build. The crucial caveat: the US is demanding a LONGER truce than the 10-day proposal, so this is de-escalation-in-progress, not a signed deal - the marginal headline risk now runs both ways. FX transmission: (1) CAD is the clearest loser - the terms-of-trade premium that made it last week's winner is gone with crude near $84 and no domestic hawkish leg to replace it; USD/CAD LONG (HIGH) is the cleanest expression. (2) The JPY gets fundamental relief - the energy importer benefits most, and BoJ Jul 31 (trend 1.9%) arms the hawks - but spot still ~163.8 as the dollar is firm into the Fed. (3) The USD's bid rotates from haven to policy - hike odds up to ~34% (Sept ~82%); DXY long tilt. (4) Gold and silver bled off the haven bid to $4,046 / $57.68 - XAU/XAG downgraded to RANGE (short tilt). (5) NZD and GBP lose their fuel-CPI engine as the petrol pass-through stops renewing, softening both forward paths. (6) The DAX gets an energy-cost tailwind - GER40 flips to a long tilt. Every oil-linked leg keys off the same binary - and today it broke to the downside. If the 10-day truce collapses, it all snaps back.
